correctness.rationale: The minimum lattice Manhattan length at least five excludes any extra common neighbor of an opposite pair and any triple overlap between distinct four-neighbor sets. Removing the indicated free triangle/tetrahedron pair and then the opposite-edge/triangle pair at every vertex is a valid \(2N\)-step elementary collapse. The surviving diamond-triangulation planes are translated by L; their parity-plane orbit count is one or two and all quotients are orientable tori. Explicit f-vector and integral homology follow. Finite checker independently verifies each elementary collapse, link and homology sample; it is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A periodic square-grid graph is a canonical geometric/combinatorial object. The theorem determines the complete integral topological type of its open-neighborhood complex for a motivated high-injectivity class of all rank-two lattice quotients, including noncyclic twisted families beyond existing circulant classifications. The PL surface core and exact \(2N\) elementary collapses are structurally stronger than Betti numbers and explain why graph bipartiteness forces two torus components; twist k can switch the outcome even when the original vertex number is fixed. This is not an arbitrary finite slice.
